metadata.scenario_context: Mike, Kim, and Emily, who are university students and schoolmates, have recently partnered to start a company that has just secured a significant investment. They are preparing to celebrate. Recent news indicates that the government is introducing new policies to assist businesses, which they are planning to discuss.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Maldives have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss going to a barbecue buffet.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking... we should celebrate our investment with a barbecue buffet. What do you think? 

Also, I’ve been curious about the recent news. Do you think people really have confidence in the press these days?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
A barbecue buffet sounds fun... but maybe we could do something more unique? I mean, there are some great local places we could check out. 

As for the press... well, honestly, I don’t have much confidence in it. People in the Maldives see it as unreliable, you know? Just feels like we can’t trust what we read.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that a unique place might be fun, but I really think a barbecue buffet would be a great way to celebrate. It's casual and delicious. 

About the press, I don't understand why people feel that way. In China, we have a great deal of confidence in the press. It provides reliable information. Why do you think it’s different for you?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I see what you mean about the barbecue buffet; it does sound enjoyable and casual for celebrating our achievement together. 

But regarding the press, I think it’s just one of those differences in perception. Deep down, we are all the same. People are pretty much motivated by the same things—wanting reliable information. It’s just that in different places, those experiences shape our views differently. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us; we all want trust and transparency, after all.
